facts.raw_span: a two-year history of gradually progressive abdominal distension
denied pain, vaginal bleeding, or systemic symptoms
no personal or family history of cancer
BMI was 20.5 kg/m2
blood pressure 125/85 mmHg
pulse 89/min
SpO2 95% on room air
abdomen was markedly distended with a palpable mass rising approximately 3 cm above the umbilicus
Transvaginal ultrasound demonstrated an 18 cm diameter ovarian tumor
hemoglobin 10.1 g/dL with a microcytic profile (MCV 73.2 fL)

Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen and pelvis revealed a large, fluid-filled lesion measuring 19.3 × 6.2 × 21 cm, located in the pelvis and mid-abdomen, displacing the uterus and compressing the aorta and inferior vena cava

concepts.why: The patient has a large, fluid-filled ovarian tumor with a high specificity finding on transvaginal ultrasound and contrast-enhanced CT.

rationales.F01: Abdominal distension is a common symptom of ovarian tumors, but it is not specific to any particular type of ovarian tumor.
rationales.F08: A palpable mass in the abdomen is a strong indicator of an ovarian tumor, particularly when combined with abdominal distension.
rationales.F09: The presence of an 18cm diameter ovarian tumor on transvaginal ultrasound is a strong indicator of an ovarian tumor.
rationales.F10: Microcytic anemia is a common finding in iron deficiency anemia, which may be related to chronic blood loss or other conditions.
rationales.F12: The large, fluid-filled lesion on CT scan is consistent with a mucinous or serous cystadenoma of the ovary, and the location and size of the lesion are consistent with an ovarian tumor.

frontier_selector.rationale: The large, fluid-filled lesion with a 1.5mm wall and no septations or solid components, as seen on CT, is more suggestive of a mucinous cystadenoma, which is a type of ovarian tumor that can present with a large, fluid-filled mass.
